title: Belrise Industries Sees Margin Improvement as Cost Pressures Ease, Stock Rallies 97% in One Year
excerpt: The Pune-based auto components maker reported a 27% revenue jump in Q1 and is raising Rs 1,200 crore via QIP to fund expansion into defence and new vehicle platforms.
body:
• Belrise Industries reported a 27% year-on-year revenue jump to Rs 2,262 crore in Q1 FY26, with profit after tax surging 56% to Rs 112 crore.
  • The stock has rallied 97% over the past year and trades 70% above its IPO listing price, though EBITDA margins declined slightly to 12.4% from 13.5% on rising costs.
  • The company launched a Rs 1,200 crore Qualified Institutional Placement to fund capacity expansion, defence diversification, and potential acquisitions.
  • HSBC expects Belrise's profits to grow at a 24% CAGR through FY29, while Jefferies has initiated coverage with a buy rating.

Strong Q1 Sets the Tone

Belrise Industries, the Pune-based auto components manufacturer that made its stock market debut earlier this year, delivered a strong June quarter. Revenue rose 27% year-on-year to Rs 2,262 crore, driven by manufacturing revenue of Rs 1,832 crore — a 29% increase supported by higher content per vehicle, increased order rollouts from its proprietary product portfolio, and the commissioning of a new Chennai facility.

Profit after tax came in at Rs 112 crore, up 56% from the year-ago quarter. The bottom line benefited from a dramatic improvement in the company's balance sheet: using IPO proceeds, Belrise repaid Rs 1,596 crore in debt, slashing its net debt-to-equity ratio from 0.98x to 0.16x.

The one blemish was a slight contraction in EBITDA margins to 12.4% from 13.5% a year earlier, impacted by rising input costs. However, EBITDA in absolute terms still grew 17% to Rs 280 crore, and management has expressed optimism that cost pressures are now largely behind the company.

"Profit after tax came in at Rs 112 crore, up 56% from the year-ago quarter."

From IPO Newcomer to Market Darling

Belrise listed on the NSE at Rs 100 per share, an 11% premium to its IPO price of Rs 90. The Rs 2,150 crore IPO was subscribed 41 times, signaling strong institutional appetite. Since then, the stock has climbed to around Rs 255, delivering a 97% return over the past year and trading more than 70% above its listing price.

The rally has attracted attention from global brokerages. Jefferies initiated coverage with a buy rating and a target price of Rs 135, citing attractive valuations at 0.8x PEG compared to the Indian auto parts sector average of 1.8x. HSBC expects manufacturing revenues to grow from Rs 7,700 crore to Rs 11,400 crore over FY26 through FY29, with profit after tax growing at a 24% compound annual growth rate to Rs 960 crore.

Expansion and Diversification

To fund its next growth phase, Belrise launched a Rs 1,200 crore QIP in July with a floor price of Rs 230.79 per share. The capital raise, which could dilute equity by up to 5.78%, is earmarked for capacity expansion and potential inorganic growth.

The company's expansion strategy extends beyond its traditional automotive business. Belrise has established relationships with one Israeli and two Indian defence OEMs as part of a diversification push into defence and aerospace components. New facilities in Pune and Bhiwadi are on track to ramp up operations in the coming quarters, adding to the recently commissioned Chennai plant.

Recent acquisitions of H-One India and the plastic components business of Mag Filters are being integrated, bringing specialized capabilities in high-tensile steel fabrication and filtration technology. These additions enhance Belrise's relevance across passenger vehicles, commercial vehicles, and two-wheelers.

Risks to Watch

Not everyone is uniformly bullish. MarketsMojo downgraded the stock to Hold in May, noting that the P/E ratio of approximately 39x has moved the valuation from attractive to fair territory. The company remains heavily dependent on its top customer — believed to be Bajaj Auto — and related-party transactions accounted for 26% of revenues and 29% of purchases in the nine months through December 2024.

Any weakening in two-wheeler demand, which represents a significant portion of Belrise's business, could pressure growth. But for now, the combination of a clean balance sheet, margin recovery trajectory, and diversification into higher-value segments has kept institutional investors interested.
